essential_question: How do area models and place value explain what happens when we multiply larger numbers?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate independent understanding of multi-digit multiplication across concept, representation, and application.
Analyze a plausible error involving multi-digit multiplication, correct it, and explain why the correction works.

success_criteria: The learner completes the task about multi-digit multiplication.
The learner shows a model, calculation, or documented process rather than a bare answer.
The learner checks the work against the criteria and names one next step.
materials: notebook, paper, or an accessible digital equivalent
pencil or an accessible response tool
the unit representation set: open area models; partial-product recording; place-value decomposition
household or classroom objects may substitute for any named manipulative

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Confirm accommodations, response mode, and extended time before starting. Read the criteria for multi-digit multiplication aloud if helpful. None of this changes the standard being assessed.
The learner explains multi-digit multiplication and shows it with a model or representation.
The learner applies multi-digit multiplication to a situation not worked in class and shows the process.
The learner diagnoses a plausible error involving multi-digit multiplication, corrects it, and connects the idea to another idea from the unit.
The learner names one secure skill and one next question. The score is recorded as one evidence source among several.

student_activity: The learner completes the unit assessment independently, showing concept, representation, application, error analysis, connection, and reflection evidence for multi-digit multiplication.
formative_check: Submit the assessment with reasoning shown, then name one secure skill and one next question.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated target for multi-digit multiplication: accuracy, the quality of the model or reasoning, and the revision. Accept any valid approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

target_misconception.pattern: Finds only two of the four partial products when multiplying two two-digit numbers.
target_misconception.diagnostic_probe: Your area model has four regions. How many products did you write?
target_misconception.repair_move: Label all four regions of the area model and check each one off as it is computed.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Record that a prerequisite for multi-digit multiplication is not secure (multiplication facts within 100). Do not reteach it now; this task must stay unsupported to count as independent evidence.

Record the pattern neutrally: Finds only two of the four partial products when multiplying two two-digit numbers. Do NOT deliver the diagnostic probe or the repair move during this task. Both are scheduled for the day-17 reassessment.
Note that the recorded reasoning for multi-digit multiplication is thin. Ask for the reasoning only after the learner has finished and submitted the task.
After the task, confirm specifically that the reasoning for multi-digit multiplication was sound. Do not begin remediation.
Record the pattern for the day-17 reassessment. Do not interrupt the task to correct it.

Provide the access support. Extended time, reduced quantity, an alternate response mode, a break, or re-reading the directions never make the evidence guided and never change the standard being evidenced.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before recording multi-digit multiplication as mastered.

mastery_rule: One correct response cannot establish mastery of multi-digit multiplication. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, separated by time or by representation. Guided success is recorded as supported and is not weighted as independent evidence.
support: Do not reteach multi-digit multiplication during this task. Access supports -- extended time, reduced quantity, alternate response mode, breaks, and re-reading the directions -- are always available and do not change the standard being evidenced. Record what you observe and act on it during the day-17 reassessment or the unit's prerequisite practice. Prerequisites for this unit: multiplication facts within 100; place value to one million; the distributive property.
extension: Apply multi-digit multiplication under a new constraint, compare two strategies and justify which is more efficient, or write an original problem and its worked solution. The learner may not complete another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional read-aloud; no voice input and no camera are required at any point.
Chunk directions to one action at a time and keep a worked example visible while the learner works.
Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, built, or manipulative-based responses whenever the standard allows it.
Offer reduced item counts, extended time, hidden or disabled timers, movement breaks, and a low-distraction setting.
Describe every representation in words so the lesson works with high-contrast print, screen readers, or no images at all.
Keep all diagrams static and describable; no animation, motion, or auto-advance is required to understand the mathematics.
Size interactive targets for touch and allow the whole task to be completed on a small screen or on paper.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language; an error is information about the next teaching move, never a judgment of the learner.
Allow a pause, break, or change of response mode at any time without recording it as a failure.
Do not require photographs, voice recordings, location, or any personal or family detail to complete a task.
Any task involving tools, heat, liquids, or moving about the home requires adult supervision and may be replaced with a paper alternative.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram or worked example illustrating multi-digit multiplication.
media.fallback: Every representation in this lesson is fully described in words and can be built from paper, household objects, or a plain number line. No image, video, audio, or animation is required.

evidence_record.note: Mastery decisions are made from the recorded evidence type and adult-observed result. Storing the learner's raw answers is never required by this course.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw answers, private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Notice one safe, optional example of multi-digit multiplication in daily life and describe it. No purchase, account, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

focus: the mathematical justifications in the capstone design
essential_question: How do lines, angles, and symmetry describe the shapes we design and build?
learning_objectives: Retrieve the mathematical justifications in the capstone design from memory after a delay, without speed pressure or public comparison.
Name the strategy used for the mathematical justifications in the capstone design and explain when that strategy is a good choice.
Distinguish items involving the mathematical justifications in the capstone design that are secure from those that still need work.
success_criteria: The learner completes the task about the mathematical justifications in the capstone design.
The learner shows a model, calculation, or documented process rather than a bare answer.
The learner checks the work against the criteria and names one next step.
materials: notebook, paper, or an accessible digital equivalent
pencil or an accessible response tool
the unit representation set: circles partitioned into degrees; protractor diagrams; angle decomposition diagrams
household or classroom objects may substitute for any named manipulative

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Pull items on the mathematical justifications in the capstone design and on two earlier units. Spacing matters more than volume here.
For each item, the learner names the strategy used for the mathematical justifications in the capstone design and why it fit.
Work a short fluency set on the mathematical justifications in the capstone design. Timers stay hidden or off. Accuracy and strategy are the targets; speed is not scored.
The learner scans their own work on the mathematical justifications in the capstone design for a pattern and describes it neutrally.
The learner sorts the mathematical justifications in the capstone design items into secure and not-yet-secure and picks one to revisit.

student_activity: The learner completes a mixed, untimed retrieval set covering the mathematical justifications in the capstone design and two earlier units, naming the strategy used for each item.
formative_check: Sort today's the mathematical justifications in the capstone design items into secure and not-yet-secure, and name the strategy that helped most.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated target for the mathematical justifications in the capstone design: accuracy, the quality of the model or reasoning, and the revision. Accept any valid approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

target_misconception.pattern: Continues a pattern correctly but cannot state a feature that follows from the rule.
target_misconception.diagnostic_probe: Your rule adds 3 each time. What do you notice about whether the terms are odd or even?
target_misconception.repair_move: Extend the pattern several terms and describe a property the rule did not state explicitly.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite for the mathematical justifications in the capstone design (quadrilateral categories from Grade 3), reteach with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.

Observed pattern: Continues a pattern correctly but cannot state a feature that follows from the rule. Ask: "Your rule adds 3 each time. What do you notice about whether the terms are odd or even?" Then: Extend the pattern several terms and describe a property the rule did not state explicitly.
Ask the learner to represent why the procedure for the mathematical justifications in the capstone design works before continuing to more items.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of the mathematical justifications in the capstone design, and do not start remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short spaced review rather than a longer session today.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before recording the mathematical justifications in the capstone design as mastered.

mastery_rule: One correct response cannot establish mastery of the mathematical justifications in the capstone design. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, separated by time or by representation. Guided success is recorded as supported and is not weighted as independent evidence.
support: If the learner is not yet ready for the mathematical justifications in the capstone design, return to the smallest prerequisite, reteach it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. Prerequisites for this unit: quadrilateral categories from Grade 3; measurement; addition and subtraction.
extension: Apply the mathematical justifications in the capstone design under a new constraint, compare two strategies and justify which is more efficient, or write an original problem and its worked solution. The learner may not complete another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional read-aloud; no voice input and no camera are required at any point.
Chunk directions to one action at a time and keep a worked example visible while the learner works.
Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, built, or manipulative-based responses whenever the standard allows it.
Offer reduced item counts, extended time, hidden or disabled timers, movement breaks, and a low-distraction setting.
Describe every representation in words so the lesson works with high-contrast print, screen readers, or no images at all.
Keep all diagrams static and describable; no animation, motion, or auto-advance is required to understand the mathematics.
Size interactive targets for touch and allow the whole task to be completed on a small screen or on paper.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language; an error is information about the next teaching move, never a judgment of the learner.
Allow a pause, break, or change of response mode at any time without recording it as a failure.
Do not require photographs, voice recordings, location, or any personal or family detail to complete a task.
Any task involving tools, heat, liquids, or moving about the home requires adult supervision and may be replaced with a paper alternative.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram or worked example illustrating the mathematical justifications in the capstone design.
media.fallback: Every representation in this lesson is fully described in words and can be built from paper, household objects, or a plain number line. No image, video, audio, or animation is required.

evidence_record.note: Mastery decisions are made from the recorded evidence type and adult-observed result. Storing the learner's raw answers is never required by this course.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw answers, private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Notice one safe, optional example of the mathematical justifications in the capstone design in daily life and describe it. No purchase, account, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
